problems.title: A second mixture isolates one concentration
problems.question: Mix 1 litre of type I with 2 litres of type II to obtain 16%. Add 3 more litres of type II to obtain 17%. Find type I concentration.
problems.idea: The added three litres account for the increase in salt amount.
steps: Subtract to get 3v=1.02-0.48=0.54, so v=0.18.

problems.title: Compare powers of the same prime
problems.question: To what power must 9⁴ be raised to obtain 27⁸?
problems.idea: Both are powers of 3.
steps: Equate the exponents: 8k=24.

problems.title: Compare individual salaries, using the correct reference
problems.question: m doctors earn n lari total; 3m drivers earn 4n total. By what percent is one doctor’s salary lower than one driver’s?
problems.idea: Divide each total by its worker count.
steps: Doctor/driver=(n/m)/(4n/(3m))=3/4.
The reduction from the driver’s salary is 1-3/4=1/4.

problems.title: The middle angle is always below 90 degrees
problems.question: Triangle angles satisfy α≤β≤γ. Which two statements can both hold: A α>60°; B β<90°; C γ<60°; D β>90°; E α+β=γ?
problems.idea: Use their positive sum 180°.
steps: A,C,D are impossible. B always holds.
E is possible for a right triangle, for example 30°,60°,90°.
Thus B and E can hold together.

problems.title: Two equal-side triangles on a hypotenuse
problems.question: In right ABC with hypotenuse AB, K,M∈AB satisfy AK=AC and BM=BC. Find MCK.
problems.idea: Use the base angles of the two isosceles triangles.
steps: The ray CK leaves angle A/2 next to CB, while CM leaves angle B/2 next to CA.

problems.title: Compare full solution sets
problems.question: Which equations are equivalent: I |x-2|=2; II |x+2|=6; III x(x-4)=0; IV |x|+|x-4|=0?
problems.idea: Solve all four.
steps: I has roots 0,4. II has roots 4,-8. III has roots 0,4.
IV would require x=0 and x=4 simultaneously, so has no roots.
Exactly I and III have the same solution set.

problems.title: Divisors of a prime power
problems.question: How many positive divisors has 199¹⁹⁹?
problems.idea: 199 is prime.
formulas: A prime power p^k has k+1 positive divisors, p⁰ through p^k.
steps: The allowed exponents are 0,1,…,199.
There are 200 choices.

problems.title: Three lines form a right isosceles triangle
problems.question: Classify the triangle formed by y=x,y=-x,y=-19.9.
problems.idea: Find its three vertices and symmetry.
steps: The two sloping lines have slopes 1 and -1, so meet perpendicularly.
Reflection in the y-axis exchanges the other vertices, making the two legs equal.

problems.title: A perpendicular median fixes a doubled hypotenuse
problems.question: In right ABC, C=90°, the B-bisector is perpendicular to median CD. Find A.
problems.idea: Resolve the sides along the B-bisector.
formulas: If BA=c,BC=a, horizontal projections of A,C are c cos(B/2),a cos(B/2).
steps: D is the midpoint of AB, so its horizontal projection from B is c cos(B/2)/2.
CD is perpendicular to the bisector, hence C,D have equal projections; this gives a=c/2.
A right triangle with hypotenuse twice BC has sinA=1/2.

problems.title: Reflecting an incenter into the circumcenter
problems.question: ABC is obtuse isosceles with AB=BC. I,O are its incenter,circumcenter, and AC is the perpendicular bisector of OI. Find B.
problems.idea: A,C are equidistant from O and I, so two triangles are congruent.
formulas: AO=AI,CO=CI; AOC and AIC share AC and are congruent by SSS.
steps: Thus their angles at O and I are equal.
For obtuse B, minor central angle AOC=360°-2B. The incenter formula gives AIC=90°+B/2.

problems.title: A sum of two completed squares
problems.question: If x²+9y²+2x+6y+2=0, find xy.
problems.idea: Complete both squares.
steps: The equation becomes (x+1)²+(3y+1)²=0.
Both squares vanish: x=-1,y=-1/3.
Their product is 1/3.

problems.title: A quartic factorization valid for every a
problems.question: Factor a⁴+a²+1.
problems.idea: Insert the middle square to use conjugates.
steps: Apply a difference of squares.

problems.title: Two sets of multiples in a two-digit interval
problems.question: Count two-digit positive integers divisible by 7 or 9.
problems.idea: Add the two counts and subtract their overlap.
formulas: Count multiples of d from 10 to 99: ⌊99/d⌋-⌊9/d⌋.
steps: There are 14-1=13 multiples of 7 and 11-1=10 multiples of 9.
Their common multiple in this range is 63, so subtract 1.

problems.title: A small circle tangent inside a 60-degree wedge
problems.question: Two radii of a large circle make 60° and are tangent to a smaller circle internally tangent to the large one. The small radius is r. Find the large radius.
problems.idea: The small centre lies on the angle bisector.
formulas: r=d sin30°=d/2, where d is the centre distance.
steps: Thus d=2r.
Internal tangency gives the large radius R=d+r=3r.

problems.title: A tangent cuts a constant-perimeter corner
problems.question: A triangle has sides 17,18,19. A tangent to its incircle cuts the two larger sides, removing the triangle at their common vertex. Find that small triangle’s perimeter.
problems.idea: Use equal tangent lengths from the shared vertex.
formulas: Tangent length from that vertex=s-17, with s=(17+18+19)/2=27.
steps: The distance to each original incircle contact is 27-17=10.
If the new tangent meets the larger sides at X,Y, its length equals (10-AX)+(10-AY) by equal tangents.
The corner triangle perimeter is AX+AY+XY=20.

problems.title: Coefficient sum is evaluation at one
problems.question: Expand (a²+b²)³-(a³+b³)² conceptually and find the sum of its coefficients.
problems.idea: Substitute a=b=1.
formulas: For any polynomial P, coefficient sum=P(1,1).
steps: The result is (1+1)³-(1+1)²=8-4=4.

problems.title: Multiply monomial powers
problems.question: Simplify (2x³y)²(xy²)³.
problems.idea: Multiply exponents within powers and add them across factors.
steps: The first factor is 4x⁶y² and second x³y⁶.
Their product is 4x⁹y⁸.
problems.answer: 4x⁹y⁸; none of the preceding printed expressions.

problems.title: A circle centre is equally far from two tangent lines
problems.question: A circle touches x=1 and y=2. Which listed point can be its centre?
problems.idea: Its two perpendicular distances must be equal.
steps: At (19,20) the distances are both 18.
The other listed points have unequal distances from the two lines.

problems.title: A tangent and a secant through a right isosceles triangle
problems.question: From exterior A draw tangent AB and secant ACD. Triangle BCD is isosceles right. Find BAC.
problems.idea: Use the possible 90°,45°,45° angles and their arcs.
formulas: The exterior tangent-secant angle is half the difference of its intercepted arcs.
steps: If the right angle were at B, CD would be a diameter and the tangent at the arc midpoint B would be parallel to CD, giving no finite intersection A.
In the other two possible placements, the intercepted far and near arcs differ by 90°.

problems.title: An interior angle exceeds an exterior angle
problems.question: A triangle interior angle and an exterior angle have ratio 5:4. Find its largest interior angle.
problems.idea: The interior angle cannot be at a different vertex.
formulas: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
steps: At a different vertex the exterior angle would exceed the chosen interior angle, contrary to ratio 5:4.
Thus the two are adjacent supplements: 5t+4t=180°, so t=20°.
The interior angle is 100°; the other two sum to 80° and are each smaller.

problems.title: Circumcenter of an intercept triangle
problems.question: The line y=-(4/3)x+8 cuts a triangle off the coordinate axes. Find its circumcenter.
problems.idea: The origin is the right-angle vertex.
formulas: A right triangle’s circumcenter is the hypotenuse midpoint.
steps: The intercepts are (6,0),(0,8).
Their midpoint is (3,4).

problems.title: Solve for the reciprocals first
problems.question: 1/(x-y)+1/(x+y)=4/9 and 1/(x-y)-1/(x+y)=2/9. Find xy.
problems.idea: Add and subtract the two equations.
steps: Thus x-y=3,x+y=9.
The solution is x=6,y=3, which satisfies the nonzero-denominator restrictions.

problems.title: Two equal journey times
problems.question: A 432 km route takes equal time on its first 7/12 and last 5/12. Speed drops by 24 km/h on the last part. Find total time.
problems.idea: Each time interval is the same unknown t.
steps: 24=72/t, so t=3 hours.
There are two such intervals.

problems.title: The average of twenty angles
problems.question: Ten distinct lines pass through a point, making 20 consecutive angles. Which must be true?
problems.idea: Their sum is one full turn.
steps: At least one angle is at most the average 18°.
It is therefore strictly below 20°.
Equal 18° gaps show why strictly below 18° is not guaranteed.
problems.answer: At least one angle is less than 20° (choice f).

problems.title: Find a midpoint before its endpoint
problems.question: A,B,C,D occur in order on a line, AD=25,BC=5. A is 6 farther than D from the midpoint of BC. Find CD.
problems.idea: Use coordinates A=0,D=25 and midpoint P.
steps: Thus p=15.5.
C is 2.5 to the right of P, so C=18.
